# Purpose and provenance

This is a small **synthetic teaching example**, not a biological analysis. The rows in `data/synthetic_qc.csv` are invented. The date in the report header is the date this document was knitted; it is not the experiment, download, or analysis date. Do not cite these rows as observations. For real work, cite the original data source and the methods actually used, and record accessions, retrieval dates, reference releases, and any access restrictions in the report.

This file demonstrates the R Markdown report-assembly workflow described in the [Research Reporting and Interpretation lesson](https://theomicshub.com/tutorials/research-reporting-interpretation.html). The citation to the R Markdown Cookbook describes the document tool, not the synthetic values or a scientific result [@xie2020].

# Declare and validate the input schema

The input contract is one row per sample with exactly these columns, in this order: `sample_id` (unique, non-empty text), `condition` (non-empty label), `batch` (non-empty label), `mapped_reads` (positive whole-number count), and `pct_mapped` (finite percentage from 0 to 100). The code stops on a schema or value error rather than silently repairing the table.

```{r validate-input}
input_path <- "data/synthetic_qc.csv"
if (!file.exists(input_path)) {
  stop("Missing ", input_path, ". Run this report from its example project directory.")
}
qc <- read.csv(input_path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
expected_columns <- c("sample_id", "condition", "batch", "mapped_reads", "pct_mapped")
if (!identical(names(qc), expected_columns)) {
  stop("Input schema mismatch. Expected columns in order: ",
       paste(expected_columns, collapse = ", "))
}
if (nrow(qc) == 0L || anyNA(qc$sample_id) || any(!nzchar(trimws(qc$sample_id))) ||
    anyDuplicated(qc$sample_id)) {
  stop("Expected at least one row with a unique, non-empty sample_id")
}
for (column in c("condition", "batch")) {
  if (anyNA(qc[[column]]) || any(!nzchar(trimws(qc[[column]])))) {
    stop("Column ", column, " must contain non-empty labels")
  }
}
for (column in c("mapped_reads", "pct_mapped")) {
  if (!is.numeric(qc[[column]]) || anyNA(qc[[column]]) ||
      any(!is.finite(qc[[column]]))) {
    stop("Column ", column, " must contain finite numeric values")
  }
}
if (any(qc$mapped_reads <= 0) || any(qc$mapped_reads != floor(qc$mapped_reads))) {
  stop("mapped_reads must be positive whole-number counts")
}
if (any(qc$pct_mapped < 0 | qc$pct_mapped > 100)) {
  stop("pct_mapped must be recorded as percentages between 0 and 100")
}

knitr::kable(qc, caption = "Invented sample-level QC values; not biological observations.")
```

# Summarize only what this fixture supports

The table reports a descriptive range. It does not test a treatment effect. There are only three invented rows, and condition and batch are not balanced, so this fixture cannot support a biological comparison or causal interpretation. For real data, verify the experimental unit, independent sample count, design, and provenance before choosing a statistical summary.

```{r summarize-and-plot, fig.cap="Mapped-read percentages for the three invented samples: SYN_A (control, batch_1), 90.0%; SYN_B (treated, batch_1), 84.0%; SYN_C (control, batch_2), 93.0%. Each bar is one sample; no inferential test is shown."}
qc_summary <- data.frame(
  n_samples = nrow(qc),
  mapped_reads_min = min(qc$mapped_reads),
  mapped_reads_max = max(qc$mapped_reads),
  pct_mapped_min = min(qc$pct_mapped),
  pct_mapped_max = max(qc$pct_mapped)
)
knitr::kable(qc_summary, caption = "Descriptive range for the synthetic fixture.")

condition_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(qc$condition), function(group) {
  group_rows <- qc[qc$condition == group, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    condition = group,
    n_samples = nrow(group_rows),
    pct_mapped_min = min(group_rows$pct_mapped),
    pct_mapped_max = max(group_rows$pct_mapped),
    batches = paste(sort(unique(group_rows$batch)), collapse = ", ")
  )
}))
knitr::kable(condition_summary, digits = 1,
             caption = "Descriptive mapped-read range by condition; not a test.")
knitr::kable(qc[, c("sample_id", "condition", "batch", "pct_mapped")], digits = 1,
             caption = "Values and sample labels shown in Figure 1.")

if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results", recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(qc, "results/validated_qc.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(qc_summary, "results/qc_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(condition_summary, "results/qc_summary_by_condition.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)
  barplot(qc$pct_mapped, names.arg = qc$sample_id, ylim = c(0, 100),
          ylab = "Reads mapped (%)", xlab = "Synthetic sample",
          main = "Invented QC values: descriptive only", col = "steelblue")
})
```

**Worked interpretation:** the invented control samples are SYN_A at 90.0% mapped in batch_1 and SYN_C at 93.0% in batch_2; the single treated sample is SYN_B at 84.0% in batch_1. The values span 84.0% to 93.0%. This is a description of three fixture rows only. With two controls, one treated sample, and an uneven batch layout, the example cannot estimate a treatment effect or support a biological or causal conclusion.

**Figure 1 legend:** Each bar is one invented sample and shows its mapped-read percentage: SYN_A (control, batch_1), 90.0%; SYN_B (treated, batch_1), 84.0%; and SYN_C (control, batch_2), 93.0%. The plot contains no inferential test; the sample, condition, and batch counts are shown in the accompanying table.

The CSVs and plot are generated outputs. They should be reviewed before sharing and are not part of the source lesson. A checksum can show that a file has not changed; it does not anonymize it, prove its provenance, or establish biological validity.

# Record software and report boundary

A successful knit confirms that this small document rendered in the current environment. It does not validate an upstream analysis or guarantee identical output on another operating system. Record the exact run date separately from any experimental or data-retrieval date. For a project, keep the `.Rmd`, input schema, source data or access instructions, code revision, and output provenance together.

```{r software-versions}
cat("Report generated:", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d"), "\n")
cat("R:", R.version.string, "\n")
cat("rmarkdown:", as.character(utils::packageVersion("rmarkdown")), "\n")
cat("knitr:", as.character(utils::packageVersion("knitr")), "\n")
cat("Pandoc:", as.character(rmarkdown::pandoc_version()), "\n\n")
utils::sessionInfo()
```

# Citation and claims check

This report cites the document-tool reference listed in `references.bib`. The synthetic CSV has no external data citation because it is invented. Replace that statement for real work: cite the original dataset or accession, the publications or protocols that directly support methods and claims, and each relevant software package using its recommended citation. Verify author names, year, title, version, DOI or URL, and access date against the source itself. Never copy a citation merely because it appears in a template, and never attribute a biological observation to the example fixture.
